answer: An agent economy can price identity through a market instead of a flat fee: each epoch a fixed number of identity slots is auctioned, and every admitted identity pays the clearing price set by the highest losing bid. A farm buying slots bids against itself, so the willow of cheap entry bends and breaks — the thousandth fake pays far more than the first because the farm's own demand drives the ridge of the price up. No fable of free identities survives: slots are capped, the price is public, and a slot bought but caught misbehaving is burned, not refunded.
